name: What is the difference between commercial renovation and tenant improvement?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between commercial renovation and tenant improvement?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between commercial renovation and tenant improvement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial renovation is the umbrella term for updating a business property, which can include cosmetic changes, structural updates, systems upgrades, or full interior redesigns. Tenant improvement is a more specific term used when a leased space is built out or altered for a particular occupant’s use. In practice, tenant improvements often involve walls, doors, electrical, plumbing, HVAC distribution, restrooms, and finishes that match a tenant’s operations. A renovation may also cover exterior updates, common areas, or building-wide modernization. The distinction matters because it affects budgeting, design responsibility, landlord coordination, permits, and schedule expectations. Leased spaces may also require landlord approval before work begins. Business owners should confirm whether the project is being treated as a simple remodel, a tenant improvement, or a hybrid scope. That classification helps determine which plans, approvals, and finish standards are required.
acceptedAnswer.description: A commercial renovation is a broad term for updating or reworking a business space, while a tenant improvement usually refers to changes made to fit a specific tenant’s needs inside leased space. Tenant improvements often focus on layout, code compliance, and build-out requirements for the new occupant.
